Data:Wc.json.Label: Writing-Case
Data:Wc.json.Desc: 'A sturdy brass-cornered writing-case which has been of service to at least three Librarians of the House. [Use your Writing-Case in a Desk with Ink to invite Visitors to a Salon. To invite villagers, add your Writing-Case as a discussion subject when you visit them in Brancrug.]
Data:Wc.json.comments: Ambitting here depends on some semi-intentional behaviour - the wc occurs earlier than skills - and might break later.'

Data:Wc.markeraspect.json.label: wcma
Data:Wc.markeraspect.json.desc: NO NEED TO LOCALISE THIS Marker aspect for writing case so it can go in village slots without confusing non-HOL players. Cleaner to use 'blank' but then we get branch creep.

Data:Wc.send.enabled.json.label: A Gift from Dr Blackwood
Data:Wc.send.enabled.json.startdescription:
A package from Dr Serena Blackwood, who once also served as Librarian here:

'Librarian: I remember very well how remote Brancrug is from the world. In Alexandria, I have both a telegraph office and more company than I can easily stand. You will, I think, make better use of this than I.

Best wishes
 Serena'

xexts.scrutiny: Stout English elm - or stout once. It hasn't been used in years. It'd probably snap in two.
Supple Cornish ash - or supple once. It hasn't been used in years. It'd probably snap in two.
Good Welsh yew once… now it's rotting from the inside out.

Data:Weapon.crossbow.json.Label: Crossbow
Data:Weapon.crossbow.json.Desc: An antique crossbow from Hush House's early Baronial period.

xexts.scrutiny: Still in excellent condition. In the unlikely event I ever need to fend off robber knights, I could do worse than this.

Data:Weapon.foil.dearday.json.Label: Dearday's Foil
Data:Weapon.foil.dearday.json.Desc: A pin-sharp length of flexible steel. The blade is inscribed DEARDAY.

xexts.scrutiny: Dearday was one-half of the Edge dyad that Natalia Brulleau hoped to lure to Hush House - to learn from them or to imprison them?

Data:Weapon.foil.torgue.json.Label: Torgue's Foil
Data:Weapon.foil.torgue.json.Desc: A pin-sharp length of flexible steel. The blade is inscribed TORGUE.

xexts.scrutiny: Torgue was one-half of the Edge dyad that Natalia Brulleau hoped to lure to Hush House - to learn from them or to imprison them?

Data:Weapon.hendrik.json.Label: Hendrik's Blade
Data:Weapon.hendrik.json.Desc: A long hunting knife, or a short close-quarters sword. A plaque reads 'Hendrik Dewulf, 1525'

xexts.scrutiny: If the blade is real and the date correct, Hendrik must have borne this weapon during his time on the Continent, long before he ever became first Baron Brancrug… perhaps even in the 1527 Sack of Rome, which apparently provoked his spiritual crisis and brought him, eventually, to Brancrug.

Data:Weapon.leaf.grail.json.Label: Red Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.leaf.grail.json.Desc: A leaf-shaped wooden sword of considerable age.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is birch; the hilt is marked with red ochre.

Data:Weapon.leaf.moth.json.Label: Dappled Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.leaf.moth.json.Desc: A leaf-shaped wooden sword of considerable age.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is poplar; the hilt is marked with blackthorn and holly.

Data:Weapon.pistols.flintlock.json.Label: Matched Flintlock Pistols
Data:Weapon.pistols.flintlock.json.Desc: A pair of pistols - the style and maker's mark suggest late seventeenth century.  The initials 'MD' are marked in silver, above the wolf-sejant of the Barons Brancrug.

xexts.scrutiny: There is a story that Musgrave Dewulf died in a secret duel with a 'Welsh visitor'. There is nothing to suggest that this is true, or that these pistols were ever used in a duel… but the date might match, and one might speculate.

Data:Weapon.practice.azita.json.Label: Azita's Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.practice.azita.json.Desc: A varnished length of wood. The name AZITA is inlaid in silver.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is Cornish oak. This is one of the newer items in the practice room - no older than the current century.

Data:Weapon.practice.fraser.json.Label: Fraser's Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.practice.fraser.json.Desc: A varnished length of wood. The name FRASER has been carved into the flat.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is dark ash. The practice weapon has seen considerable use, and is notched and battered - it must be more than fifty years old.

Data:Weapon.practice.grail.json.Label: Red Quarterstaff
Data:Weapon.practice.grail.json.Desc: A long staff marked with bands of red.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is birch; the bands are marked with red ochre.
The hilt is charred, as if Greene had held it over a candle-flame.

Data:Weapon.practice.mehrdad.json.Label: Mehrad's Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.practice.mehrdad.json.Desc: A varnished length of wood. The name MEHRAD is inlaid in gold.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is Cornish oak. This is one of the newer items in the practice room - no older than the current century.

Data:Weapon.practice.moth.json.Label: Dappled Quarterstaff
Data:Weapon.practice.moth.json.Desc: A long staff marked with bands of black and white.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is poplar; the bands are blackthorn and holly.

Data:Weapon.practice.natalia.json.Label: Natalia's Practice Sword
Data:Weapon.practice.natalia.json.Desc: A varnished length of wood. The name NATALIA has been carved into the flat.

xexts.scrutiny: The wood is dark ash. The practice weapon has seen considerable use, and is notched and battered - it must be more than fifty years old.

Data:Weapon.swords.sebastian.json.Label: Sebastian's Swords
Data:Weapon.swords.sebastian.json.Desc: Matching eighteenth-century cutlasses. The initials SD are engraved on the blade near the hilt.

xexts.scrutiny: The hilt is bone; the guard is brass, decorated rather racily with nymphs pursued by satyrs. These were not regulation Royal Navy pattern, and must have been gifts or commissions by Captain Sebastian Dewulf, last of the Dewulf line, who died in action at Quiberon Bay.

Data:Weapons.td.bokken.json.Label: Bokken: Captain Torgue and Mistress Dearday
Data:Weapons.td.bokken.json.Desc: Souvenirs from the East, heavily padded.

xexts.scrutiny: Treasured items left behind by the occupants of the cell during their inglorious career on the high seas. Procured by Governor Collers as a gift for the occupants of the cell, in the hope it would induce better behaviour.

Data:Weapons.td.cudgels.json.Label: Cudgels: Dyddgu and St Twrog
Data:Weapons.td.cudgels.json.Desc: Very old iron cudgels, recently and heavily padded.

xexts.scrutiny: Retrieved from Gladwyn Lake and returned to the cell's occupants as a reward for good behaviour.

Data:Weapons.td.wasters.json.Label: Wasters: Darling-Dear and Father Turk
Data:Weapons.td.wasters.json.Desc: Wooden swords of recent manufacture, never used.

xexts.scrutiny: Provided to the occupants of the cell, who clearly disdained and never used them.
